A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dynamical chiral symmetry is more easily broken in (2+ 1)-dimensional QED than in (3+1)-dimension QED.

the dynamical chiral symmetry breakdown is more easily suppressed in QED{sup 3}, and the critical fermion number N{sub c}=3 is reduced to 2, which is consistent with the recent numerical simulation results.
the dynamical chiral symmetry is more likely to be broken in QED{sup 3} with a smaller number of fermion flavors and at a smaller chemical potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fermion mass is strongly suppressed by finite density or impurity scattering, which can be used to explain the experimental observation of a large critical flavor number for dynamical chiral symmetry in the QCD phase diagram.
